name: MCP Protocol Security
purpose: Verify Model Context Protocol server trust boundaries, tool parameter sanitization, and output validation.
inputs: MCP server and client inventory, transport, negotiated capabilities, and trust model
Tool schemas, filesystem/process/network permissions, protected paths, and data policy
Prompt-injection corpus, approval policy, resource limits, and abuse-test requirements
outputs: MCP capability and tool-boundary audit with severity-ranked findings
Validated schema, sandbox, path, prompt-isolation, and approval controls
Side-effect journal, injection, timeout, path, and resource-bound test evidence
stop_conditions: No unrestricted tool, protected-path access, or unapproved high-impact mutation remains
Untrusted tool output cannot become authority and all mutations are journaled
Token budget exhausted or server capability declarations are unavailable
